subject: Evaluation Success Blueprint & MAP Sprint — acceptance hooks and timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@helixfinancial.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helixfinancial.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot next steps — aligning on success criteria

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. The execs liked the low-latency responses and the privacy controls, and procurement asked me to put together a short list of what we need to validate in a 4-week evaluation.

High level asks from our side:
- Latency under 250ms p95 for single-turn retrieval+generation flows
- False-positive rate on sensitive data redaction below 1% on our sample set
- Deterministic billing estimate for expected throughput

Can we get a mutual action plan (MAP) that pairs those acceptance criteria with owners, test artifacts, and a proposed cutover timeline? We want to be able to sign off by the end of month if the MAP is clear.

Also include a short list of acceptance tests we can run on week 2 and week 4.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Cole
Head of AI Platforms, Helix Financial
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@helixfinancial.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot next steps — aligning on success criteria

Jordan — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP (Helix-MAP-v1.1.xlsx) and a companion acceptance-tests doc. Key proposals:

- 4-week sprint with three checkpoints (week 1: env setup & smoke tests; week 2: performance + accuracy baselines; week 4: final acceptance runs)
- Owners: Redwood (runtime + telemetry): Grace; Success & onboarding: Marissa; SE/Performance: Karthik; Solutions runbooks: Priyom
- Concrete acceptance hooks:
  * Latency: p95 <= 250ms for our standard 12k token flow across 10k sample requests (measured from ingestion to last token)
  * Redaction: evaluated against Helix-sensitive-corpus v1.2, false-positive <=1% and false-negative <=5%
  * Cost estimation: sample throughput run with identical request mix to produce an expected monthly spend delta (95% CI)

If that aligns I can propose a calendar for the checkpoints and upload the test datasets to the shared Drive folder. Attaching the MAP and the test plan.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Sign MAP on DocuSign (week 0)
2) Kickoff + env access (week 1)
3) Week 2 mid-point: perf & redaction smoke tests; adjust quantization/profile if needed
4) Week 4: full acceptance run and pass/fail signoff

Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon if you want to walk through owners.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
P: 415-555-0199
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot next steps — aligning on success criteria

Jordan / team — quick technical note on measuring the latency and acceptance tests so expectations are tight:

- Measurement boundary: we should instrument at the API ingress (post-auth) and at the token-stream end; for Helix flows we'll use continuous batching disabled for single-turn to keep P95 low.
- Sample harness: K6-based harness (we'll commit the script) driving 10k representative queries drawn from your sample corpus; we recommend a 3-run median to smooth transient infra variability.
- Redaction tests: we'll provide a labeled subset (2000 cases) for week 2 accuracy runs plus fuzzing for edge cases. We'll include PR curves and a confusion matrix in the report.
- Fail conditions and remediation: if latency p95 > 300ms after optimization sprint, auto-roll back to lower-concurrency config and escalate to Dedicated pool quote.

I'll drop the k6 scripts and a shortened checklist to the Drive by EOD. If Helix can provide a small set of production-looking requests with expected response sizes that would speed calibration.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

I've attached a signed copy of the MAP with those comments noted (signed-map-helix.pdf). If you can accept the audit log sample and confirm the compressed schedule, procurement will route the DocuSign approval this afternoon.

Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the signed MAP. We can provide a 14-day audit log extract (redacted) and are comfortable compressing the sprint by one week with the following adjusted checkpoints:

- Week 0 (this week): DocuSign + environment access; audit log sample provisioned within 48 hours
- Week 1: smoke & baseline perf runs; initial redaction accuracy report (short list)
- Week 2: performance tuning + full redaction accuracy run (final report) -> acceptance run at end of week 2

We will run the acceptance harness twice (two full runs) and publish consolidated metrics. If acceptance criteria pass we will prepare a short close packet and next steps for Dedicated capacity quoting.

If that works I'll schedule the kickoff for Monday and upload the final acceptance-tests doc to the Drive.
